abstract: The therapeutic application of in vitro transcribed (IVT) messenger RNA (mRNA) is constrained by double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) impurities generated by wild-type (WT) T7 RNA polymerase (RNAP). These impurities trigger innate immune responses via RIG-I and MDA5, suppressing protein translation. Conventional polymerase engineering often trades dsRNA reduction for lower transcription processivity. Here, we report engineered T7 RNAP variants that limit this trade-off. Physicochemical profiling identified variant G3, which suppresses high-molecular-weight aggregates and 3'-loopback hairpins while preserving full catalytic yield, high capping efficiency, and sequence processivity. In primary dendritic cells, N1-methylpseudouridine (N1psU)-modified mRNA produced by G3 yielded up to a three-fold increase in protein expression compared to WT T7, without inducing CD86 maturation. Systemic in vivo delivery in mice confirmed superior therapeutic expression and completely abrogated pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Functional knockouts confirmed that G3-transcribed mRNA evades cytosolic RIG-I/MDA5-mediated translational suppression by selectively eliminating inflammatory dsRNA byproducts. Together, G3 offers a superior, scalable manufacturing solution for advanced mRNA therapeutics.
